tools.name: fuast_guide
tools.description: Call this first. Returns how to build, check, deploy and share a fuast app with these tools, and the rules a fuast app must follow (file layout, server and client APIs, database, auth, UI). fuast apps are small full-stack TypeScript apps called capsules: server/index.ts and client/index.tsx, no npm

tools.name: fuast_docs
tools.description: Read one docs page as markdown (page), or search every page for words (search). With neither, lists the pages. Useful pages: capsule-api (every server and client API), database, auth, limits, storage, schedules, email, teams, examples/todo.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Lists the working starter apps a new fuast app can begin from, with what each one demonstrates. Get a template's files with get_template.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Returns the source files of one starter template as {path: content}: a complete app that passes check_app and can be sent to deploy_app as is. Change the files to build what the person asked for.

tools.name: check_app
tools.description: Builds the files, type checks them and loads the server in a sandbox, without deploying anything. Returns ok with the queries, mutations, tables and tools the app declares, or ok false with diagnostics that carry file, line and message. Call it before deploy_app and fix every diagnostic.

tools.name: deploy_app
tools.description: Deploys the files and returns the app's URL. With a connected fuast account it creates a new private app in the person's workspace, or updates the app named in app. Without an account it deploys a temporary preview and returns preview_url, claim_url and edit_token: give the person claim_url so they

tools.name: get_app_source
tools.description: Returns the source of the app's live deploy as {path: content}, with the deploy id to pass to update_app_files as expected_deploy_id. Large apps return the file list only: ask again with paths for the files you need. Secrets (.env files, env values) are never returned.

tools.name: update_app_files
tools.description: Redeploys the app with a few files changed: files maps each path to its new content, or to null to delete it. Every other file stays as it is. expected_deploy_id must be the app's live deploy (from get_app_source or the last deploy result); if someone deployed in between, nothing changes and you are

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: Lists the fuast apps the connected account can use: its own, its workspace's, and apps shared with it, with URL, sharing mode and whether the account can manage each one.

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Returns one app: URL, status, sharing, handlers, recent deploys with their ids (for rollback_app), today's usage and limits, and the names (never the values) of its env vars.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Returns recent log entries of an app, oldest first: what its handlers wrote with ctx.log, handler errors with stack traces, and platform events such as deploys. Pass the returned cursor as since to read only newer entries.

tools.name: inspect_app
tools.description: Reads one thing about a deployed app. manifest: handlers, schema, indexes, endpoints, read metrics. tables: each table with its fields and row count. rows: rows of one table (give table; at most 100 per call, continue with cursor). usage: today's counters and limits. schedules: cron schedules and th

tools.name: call_app
tools.description: Runs one query, mutation or action of a deployed app and returns its result and the log lines it wrote, so you can test what you deployed. It runs as the connected person (as: "me", the default), never as anyone else; as: "guest" runs it as a guest visitor and only works on public apps. On a preview

tools.name: share_app
tools.description: Changes who can open an app. visibility: private (the owner and invited people), workspace (everyone at the owner's company), or public (anyone with the link, guests included). invite adds people by email and sends each an email; remove takes people off the list. Do this only when the person asks fo

tools.name: set_env
tools.description: Sets or removes environment variables of an app (read in handlers as ctx.env.NAME). They take effect at once, without a deploy. Values are write-only: no tool returns them, only the names.

tools.name: rollback_app
tools.description: Makes an earlier deploy of the app live again. deploy_id comes from get_app; without it, the most recent earlier deploy that is ready. The app's data stays as it is; if that deploy's schema cannot hold the current data, nothing changes.

tools.name: delete_app
tools.description: Deletes an app and everything in it: its data, stored files, deploys, schedules and custom domains. This cannot be undone. Only the app's owner can do it, and confirm must repeat the app's slug. Do this only when the person explicitly asks for the app to be deleted.

tools.name: get_claim_link
tools.description: For a preview that deploy_app deployed without an account: returns the claim link to give to the person, the preview link, and when the preview is deleted if nobody claims it. Opening the claim link and signing in makes the app theirs.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Returns the fuast account this connection acts as: email, workspace, role, and what the connection may do. If no account is connected yet, calling it starts sign-in: call it when the person has a fuast account or wants apps deployed into their own workspace instead of as a temporary preview.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fuast_docs, check_app, list_apps, get_app, share_app · Private data: fuast_guide, fuast_docs, list_templates, get_template, check_app, deploy_app, get_app_source, update_app_files, get_app, share_app, set_env, delete_app · Public sink: fuast_guide, fuast_docs, deploy_app, share_app, whoami · Destructive: update_app_files, share_app, delete_app.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fuast_docs, check_app, list_apps, get_app, share_app · Private data: fuast_guide, fuast_docs, list_templates, get_template, check_app, deploy_app, get_app_source, update_app_files, get_app, share_app, set_env, delete_app · Public sink: fuast_guide, fuast_docs, deploy_app, share_app, whoami · Destructive: update_app_files, share_app, delete_app

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
